results.label: every VLQ value round-trips through the encoder and the decoder, including the 5-bit continuation boundaries
a VLQ group with several values decodes to those values in order
an invalid base64 character is reported as a SyntaxError rather than silently skipped
whole mapping sets round-trip, including empty lines and a name index
the map is Source Map v3 with this file as its source and no other source
the original text is embedded, byte-identical to the input
the map has no more generated lines than the code has
every mapping lands inside the generated text
the file produces a non-zero number of mappings
for every generated column the "greatest mapping not past the column" rule returns that mapping

every identifier in the generated file maps to a source position that really holds its name (1418 identifiers checked: 840 renamed references whose original name is in the map, 23 re-spelled on purpose)
renamed bindings are named in the map, so a reader can see what a short name used to be
a real stack trace from the minified file maps back to the original throw site
every mapping in every shipped file resolves inside that file — a line that exists and a column inside it (217884 mappings over 94 files)
no node was left unmapped for want of a source position (the guard has nothing to report)
with the map turned off there is no map object at all, rather than an empty one
with `includeContent:false` the map carries no original text and says so by being empty
two runs of the same file produce byte-identical code, map and names (the map is deterministic)

scope: the source map, checked with its own decoder: VLQ boundaries, whole-set round trips, mapping bounds, the spec lookup rule, truth of identifier positions, and a real stack trace mapped back to the original throw. Not validated against a third-party consumer: the tool is dependency free by design.
